sections.h2: Where to record a Licking County deed
sections.html:
Deeds and mortgages for Licking County land go to the recorder's office at 20 S. Second Street in Newark, OH 43055. Call (740) 670-5300 with questions or send a fax to (740) 670-5303. The counter is open 8 AM to 4:30 PM on weekdays, and recording runs from 8:30 AM to 4:15 PM.

Staff examine each document, assign it a unique document number and a recording time, and use that time to fix the order of filings. Records reach back to the early 1800s. Anyone can search the paper index and record books at the counter for no charge, and staff will help with the search.

Online viewing covers documents recorded since September 22, 1997, including deeds, mortgages, releases, assignments and UCC statements. Anything older is a trip to the counter.

The county's own fee sheet uses a simple formula: number of pages times $8, plus $23. A marginal reference costs $4. A $5 preservation surcharge applies per document for standard document types. Ask the recorder how the surcharge shows up in your total before you write the check.

Other charges follow the Ohio Recorders' Association fee table. Photocopies and plat copies are $1.00 plus $1.00 per page. A certified copy is $1.00 plus $1.00 per page, with a seal fee of 50 cents plus 50 cents. A document that fails the state layout rules adds $10.00 plus $10.00.

sections.h2: Documents recorded around a house sale
sections.html:
The state fee table groups a long list of instrument types under the basic page charge. These are the ones most tied to a sale, a payoff or an inheritance:

  • Warranty deeds, quit claim deeds, survivorship deeds and limited warranty deeds.
  • Executor's, administrator's, guardian's, trustee's and sheriff's deeds.
  • Certificates of transfer and transfer on death designation affidavits.
  • Mortgages, assignments, modifications, satisfactions and releases of lien.
  • Affidavits on facts relating to title, affidavits of surviving spouse and affidavits of successor trustee.
  • Memoranda of trust, powers of attorney, land contracts and easements.
  • Mechanic's liens, lis pendens notices and Medicaid estate recovery liens and their releases.

Military discharges record without a fee. Federal tax liens carry their own listed charge of $5.00.

No deed skips the auditor. Under section 319.202, the grantee or an agent declares the value conveyed, and the auditor stamps the deed with the fee. An exempt transfer needs only a stated reason.

A conveyance, exempt transfer, split or merge has to arrive by 4 p.m. to clear that day. The auditor is at 20 South Second Street, (740) 670-5040.

The seller pays the state conveyance fee at the auditor's counter. A county real property transfer tax would be collected there too, but only if commissioners enacted one under section 322.02, at no more than 30 cents per $100. Ask the auditor whether one exists before you pick a closing date. If it does, payment comes before the trip to the recorder.

sections.h2: Searching and watching Licking County records
sections.html:
The recorder runs a PaxWorld public access site at apps.lickingcounty.gov. You create an account with a username and password. Images you buy download to your computer, so allow downloads in your browser.

The same site offers an AlertMe service that sends a notice when a document is recorded in your name. That is handy for owners who worry about fraudulent filings against their property.

Title companies, law firms and banks that file often can use eRecording. The county names four vendors:

  • CSC eRecording Solutions
  • ePN, the eRecording Partners Network
  • Indecomm Global Services
  • Simplifile

Electronic filing can cut turnaround from three to five working days down to minutes or hours, and recording fees are paid electronically.

Licking County had 73,930 housing units in July 2025 and 68,620 households across the 2020 to 2024 survey years. Owned homes are valued around $275,200, and about three in four are lived in by the owner. Rent averages $1,078, and a homeowner with a loan pays about $1,693 monthly. Population rose from 178,501 in April 2020 to an estimated 185,564 in July 2025.

sections.h2: How a payoff or an inheritance shows up in the record
sections.html:
A sale usually produces more than one recorded paper. The buyer's deed goes on record, and the seller's old mortgage is cleared by a satisfaction or release that the lender files. The state sheet lists satisfaction, release, partial release and cancellation as separate document types. A marginal reference costs $4 when the recorder notes a link to an earlier filing.

Inherited property follows a different path. An executor's or administrator's deed, a certificate of transfer or a transfer on death designation affidavit can move title without a conventional sale, and each is recorded like any other deed. If the owner received Medicaid benefits, a Medicaid estate recovery lien and its release are recordable too. If one turns up in the chain of title, raise it with the title company before closing.

sections.h2: Searching old deeds and county lines
sections.html:
Licking County was carved out of Fairfield County in 1808, so the earliest history of a parcel may sit under the parent county's name. The recorder's holdings go back to the early 1800s, and staff will help a searcher read the index. Seven counties touch Licking County, so a parcel near a county line can carry a description that mentions Knox, Delaware, Franklin or another neighbor.

Acreage needs a wider look. Developers make frequent offers for farmland near New Albany. A deed search for a rural parcel should cover every transfer and any easements, and the state table lists agricultural easements and conservation easements as their own document types.

Order of steps on closing week

First the title company or attorney prepares the deed and the buyer and seller sign. Next the deed goes to the auditor for the conveyance statement and the fee. Then it moves to the recorder, who examines it, assigns the document number and sets the recording time. Last, the lender files its satisfaction for the seller's old mortgage. A seller who is not waiting on a lender payoff still needs the deed recorded before the buyer's ownership shows in the county index.

What to bring when you record in person

Bring the signed original, the fee for the page count, and proof that the auditor has already stamped the deed. Check that the document meets the state layout rules so the extra $10.00 plus $10.00 charge never applies. If you want a certified copy afterward, ask at the same visit.

faqs.q: When is the Licking County recorder open?
faqs.a: Staff are in from 8 AM until 4:30 PM on weekdays, and recording itself happens between 8:30 AM and 4:15 PM. Call (740) 670-5300 before a holiday.

faqs.q: What would a two-page Licking County deed cost to record?
faqs.a: The county sheet lists $39.00 for one to two pages, based on pages times $8 plus $23. A third page brings the fee to $47.00.

faqs.q: Is searching Licking County records free?
faqs.a: Searching the index and record books at the recorder's counter is free. The online PaxWorld site requires an account, and purchased images download from the site.

faqs.q: Do I need the auditor before I record a Licking County deed?
faqs.a: Yes, the auditor endorses the deed and collects the conveyance fee first. For same-day processing the deed must reach the auditor by 4 p.m.

faqs.q: Can a title company e-record in Licking County?
faqs.a: Yes, the recorder accepts electronic filings through four listed eRecording vendors. Recorded documents come back electronically.
